data.name: Chain_Hint
data.value: The first step that matches wins — a file next to the crew silently wins over the global one.

data.name: Tour1_Body
data.value: Studio is the desktop companion of the orkeon CLI: edit appsettings.json through validated forms, then launch crews and watch the streamed log. This short tour walks through each part.

data.name: Tour2_Body
data.value: Configuration covers the settings file — presets, typed sections, mounts, the raw JSON and a doctor diagnostic. Launch is where you run crews and browse the launch history.

data.name: Tour3_Title
data.value: The settings file, always in sight

data.name: Tour3_Body
data.value: This card shows which appsettings.json you are editing and whether it validates. It stays visible on every screen, so you always know what a save will touch.

data.name: Tour4_Body
data.value: New, open, reload, validate, save — the file-level actions live here on every configuration screen. Validation runs the same checks the runtime applies at load.

data.name: Tour5_Body
data.value: The same catalogue as orkeon init: Ollama, Docker Model Runner, OpenAI, any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, or none. Applying only pre-fills the Llm form — you review, then save.

data.name: Tour6_Body
data.value: The runtime walks four steps to find its settings. This card shows the whole chain and marks where your save target sits — no more silent surprises from a file next to the crew.

data.name: Tour7_Body
data.value: Mounts are the only folders agents can see. Pick the physical folder, the virtual path agents get, and the rights — read-only by default, with per-sub-path overrides.

data.name: Tour8_Body
data.value: The exact command line is built live from your options. Dry-run validates without side effects; Run streams the log here, line by line, and ends with the exit code.

data.name: Tour9_Body
data.value: The diagnostic runs orkeon doctor: binary, settings file, LLM reachability, mounts. Green means go; warnings tell you what to fix before a run fails.
